Subject: Follow-up: model fit & quantization tradeoffs for FinAnalytics

Hi Sophie — great to chat earlier today. Thanks again for the time and for walking us through FinAnalytics' inference priorities. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

Recap of requirements you mentioned:
- Target: throughput ~100 req/s sustained (burst to 200) for batch scoring workloads (larger prompts ~1k tokens).
- P95 latency target: under 300ms where possible; OK with slightly higher for heavy context windows on non-real-time pipelines.
- Hard requirement: no visible quality regressions vs your current baseline (open-source LLM tuned in-house).
- Security: PII redaction + SOC2 evidence required before production.

What we'll deliver for the model-fit eval:
1) 2-week model-fit POC using a representative prompt set you provided (you mentioned sample queries & redaction cases).
2) Comparative evaluation of 3 model variants (quality + throughput):
   - Llama-3-70B (fp16 baseline) — highest quality baseline we recommend for fidelity checks
   - Llama-3-33B quantized (AWQ/GPTQ candidates) — tradeoff candidate for lower cost/higher throughput
   - 13B FP8/GPTQ variant — for very latency-sensitive paths (if quality holds)
3) Quantization tradeoff matrix + recommended operating points (we'll attach a summary and a detailed spreadsheet).
4) Benchmarks: per-model latency/throughput on your representative prompts, cost estimate per 1M tokens, and quality regression metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-style scores + human spot checks).

Next steps / asks from your side:
- Send the anonymized prompt set and a small ground-truth sample (50-100 examples) for quality checks.
- Confirm preferred date for kickoff next week (we have availability Tue/Wed mornings PST).
- Any compliance contacts for SOC2 evidence sharing (so we can proactively gather the docs).

Attachments: finanalytics_requirements.pdf (your notes we pulled from the call), prompt_set_sample.tsv (sample format).

I'll loop in Dev (SE) and Aditya (solutions) for the model-fit plan and quantization tradeoffs.

Hi all — thanks for the signal, Sophie. A few technical notes ahead of the kickoff and what we'll bring to the POC: 

1) Models we'll stage (examples):
   - Llama-3-70B fp16 (baseline) — aim is to match/exceed fidelity of your 30B fine-tune where possible.
   - Llama-3-33B AWQ-4/GPTQ-4 candidates — these typically give 2-3x throughput improvements vs fp16 at a modest quality delta; we will run both AWQ and GPTQ to compare.
   - 13B FP8 / GPTQ — for the most aggressive throughput target; FP8 often helps latency but requires careful calibration.

2) Typical risk modes with AWQ/GPTQ we've seen (finance domain specifics):
   - Numeric drift: small misrepresentations of numbers when quantization impacts token probabilities for digits/decimal formats. Mitigation: targeted calibration on numeric-focused tokens and token-level temperature tuning + small human-in-the-loop checks on key cases.
   - Prompt sensitivity: quantized variants can be more brittle to prompt phrasing; mitigation: augment prompt set with paraphrases and use few-shot exemplars.
   - Safety/classification errors: downstream extraction (e.g., entity parsing) can degrade; mitigation: add a lightweight validation layer (rule-based checks) and fallback to higher-precision model on high-risk examples.

3) Evaluation plan & metrics we will produce for each model/config:
   - Automated: BLEU/ROUGE-style overlap where applicable, token-level numeric error metrics, confidence distributions, and per-prompt latency/throughput.
   - Human: spot-checks on 200 examples covering numeric tables and regulatory language.

4) Practical throughput knobs: batch size, KV cache reuse (for repeated prefixes), sequence truncation strategies, and kernel choice (we'll exercise AWQ-optimized kernels vs GPTQ). We'll include latency percentiles and cost-per-1M token.

Attachments: quant_tradeoffs.xlsx (detailed trade study template + example results). I'll upload a short benchmark report to the linked drive before the kickoff.

If that all looks good I'll prepare the kickoff agenda and Ops checklist (sample dataset, access, SOC2 contact).

—Dev
